The test image shows corn leaves with 2-3 elongated, somewhat cigar-shaped lesions with tan centers and dark brown/reddish-brown borders. These are large lesions on otherwise healthy green leaf tissue.

Comparing to the Northern Corn Leaf Blight reference collage — the top-left panel especially shows a nearly identical lesion: elongated, tan-to-brown with darker borders, on a green corn leaf. The shape, size, and coloration match well.

The lesions in the test image are:
- Elongated, irregular cigar-shaped (not small circular spots)
- Tan/straw-colored centers with darker brown margins
- No pustules (ruling out rust)
- No rectangular vein-limited shape (ruling out gray leaf spot)
- No yellow halos or target appearance (ruling out anthracnose early lesions)

This is consistent with Northern Corn Leaf Blight at an early-to-mid stage, where lesions are tan with darker borders before developing the characteristic gray sporulation.
